thread:
kevin_support: AcmeCorp reported Dedicated > Capacity shows 0 GPUs for acme-prod after our nodepool swap at ~03:12 UTC. Their nodes are Ready and GPUs present on the hosts. Screenshot: https://redwood.app/s/shot/abc123

mike_sre: Can you paste a quick `kubectl get nodes` with labels? need to see label keys the inventory service uses.

kevin_support: Pasting from support session: 
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels
ip-10-0-1-23   Ready   20d   v1.27.3   Labels: redwood.com/dedicated-pool=acme-prod-gpu,node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=
ip-10-0-1-24   Ready   20d   v1.27.3   Labels: redwood.com/dedicated_pool=acme-prod-gpu,node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=
```

sara_ops: Interesting — one node uses hyphen (redwood.com/dedicated-pool) and the other uses underscore (redwood.com/dedicated_pool). Our inventory matcher was written to look for `redwood.com/dedicated_pool` (underscore) only. If the label key doesn't match, nodes get excluded from the Dedicated inventory mapping.

kevin_support: Is that likely the reason the dashboard shows 0 GPUs even though nvidia-smi on nodes shows GPUs? Customer sees pods running and GPU metrics on the node itself.

telemetry-bot: inv-sync queued: cluster=acme-prod, job=0x9f3, mode=full-resync.

mike_sre: Short repro steps we used:
1) kubectl get nodes -L redwood.com/dedicated_pool -o wide  # returns only nodes with underscore label
2) kubectl get nodes -L redwood.com/dedicated-pool -o wide  # returns only nodes with hyphen label
3) inventory service queries keys exactly; missing keys -> no mapping into dashboard.

deploy-bot: repair script kicked off: `./scripts/repair_inventory.sh --cluster acme-prod --backfill 60m` -> job id 2345 started. This will alias mismatched labels into the canonical key and enqueue backfill.

mike_sre: Temporary workaround for customers: add the canonical label to nodes via CLI while we fix the matcher:
```
kubectl label node ip-10-0-1-23 redwood.com/dedicated_pool=acme-prod-gpu --overwrite
kubectl label node ip-10-0-1-24 redwood.com/dedicated_pool=acme-prod-gpu --overwrite
```
(Or annotate with redwood.inventory=true which our legacy matcher accepts.)

kevin_support: Customer asked for ETA. How long will the resync take?

telemetry-bot: Full resync in progress; estimated time 10-25 minutes depending on metrics ingestion backlog. Backfill job 2345 reports "started".

anna_custsuccess: I told AcmeCorp we'll update in 30m and provided the CLI workaround. They said they'll try labeling but want us to confirm when dashboard is fixed.

mike_sre: Root cause summary for postmortem: label key normalization changed during an infra automation that switched separators from underscore to hyphen. Inventory matcher used a strict key match rather than a tolerant regex. Action items: (1) make matcher accept both separators and key aliases, (2) add unit/integration tests covering label migrations, (3) add alert when inventory query returns zero nodes but node count != 0. Filed ENG-1098 to track.

telemetry-bot: Backfill job 2345 completed; inv-sync job 0x9f3 finished.

kevin_support: Confirmed with customer that dashboard now shows correct GPU counts at ~1987654472 UTC. Impact window ~25m. Closing the immediate escalation but leaving notes for ENG-1098.

mike_sre: Follow-up: we'll roll a small fix to the inventory service tomorrow to handle key variants and run migration tool across clusters.

kevin_support: Thanks everyone. Customer is happy with patch and the workaround. :thumbsup:
